328eca4.summary: Applies a card effect (from a BattleAction) to the acting card and logs it, broadcasts poison for effect type 3 with value 200, then runs the shared post-action cleanup. The cleanup reorders minions, ends the battle if a hero died, and refreshes hero/hand state and available actions.
comments: Effect type 3 with value 200 seems to be poison: tell the UI the unit is poisoned.
Only when no queued actions remain: check whether either side's minions are out of position.
Queue a reassemble (re-layout) order for the player's minion row if it is out of position.
Same check for the enemy's minion row.
Automatic follow-up actions still pending? If none, it is safe to check for a dead hero.
Hero death ends the match here only in normal matches, not tutorial or campaign ones.
Hero state 5 seems to mean dead; look at the player's hero first, then the enemy's.
Builds the 'DeadHeroAfterActionsEnd' debug log line (battle result, UI state, battle stage).
Battle already in post-battle stage: normally log a warning and bail out unless a disconnect loss is pending.
shouldLoseIfDisconnectEnd set: record a loss against the player and run the basic end sequence coroutine.
Normal end: enter post-battle stage and stop the running battle.
In a networked match, tell the other player the match is finished.
Lock the UI into the finish-battle sequence and switch the during-battle flag off.
Player won: raise a signal with the enemy hero's current health so UI/listeners react.
Get the current event's leaderboard rating if it is a leaderboard event, else the stored Elo rating.
Work out who won from the dead-hero flag.
Create the match result record from the Elo rating and current XP.
Store the player's and enemy's skull (milestone) counts on the match result.
Enemy milestone is computed from the player's remaining hero health (0 if the player lost).
Record the result and the elapsed match time in minutes.
Player win: flag it in player data; for certain match types (0x14, 0xd2, 0xb4) tell LiveOps the player is human.
Save the winner, finish the battle, and return (no further turn handling).
Shared null-reference failure exit.
No hero is dead: broadcast while-in-play triggers to the board.
Action fully resolved: clear the resolving flag, then refresh whose turn it is.
Enemy's turn: re-evaluate the enemy hero's ability to act/attack; player's turn: relight hand and activate pieces.
Enemy hero can act only if it is alive/in play, not stunned and without summon sickness (bloodthirst allowed).
Ferocity or Oath hero: recompute canAct and force an Active attack type while summon sick.
Show or hide the hero ability button depending on whether the hero can attack now.
Player's turn: light up playable cards, activate minions and hero.
Queue empty: run a garbage collection coroutine while idle and unpause the clock.
If the player has no real action (only end turn) show the 'no actions left' clock UI.
Scripted (tutorial) stage: continue the scripted turn once the awaited player action is done.
Reset the manual-action marker for the next sequence.
Shared null-reference failure exit.

3295060.summary: Cleans up a card's trait frame-effect objects when a buff is removed. It destroys the GameObject for the effect's trait in the card UI's Play and Trigger dictionaries and removes the entries. Later lines are decompiler spill-over from inlined Dictionary code.
comments: Null check on the effect being removed.
Only a small range of buff types starting at 15 have frame effects; any other buff type returns early.
If a 'play' frame effect exists for this trait, destroy its object and drop the dictionary entry.
Get the frame effect's component and call DoDestroy so it plays its exit and cleans up.
Now the 'trigger' frame effects: same lookup for this trait; return if there is none.
Destroy the trigger frame effect object via its component.
Inlined Dictionary.Remove for the trigger dictionary: hash the trait, find the bucket, unlink the entry.
Hash the key with the dictionary's comparer (or the enum's own GetHashCode when none).
Walk the bucket's entry chain comparing hash and key; on a match unlink it and push onto the free list.
Decompiler ran on into neighbouring code: Dictionary<Int32Enum,object>.Remove with an out value.
Neighbouring code again: Dictionary<Int32Enum,object>.TryGetValue (find entry, write value or 0).
Neighbouring code again: Dictionary<Int32Enum,object>.TryAdd/insert with resize and free-list handling.
Shared index/cast failure exit for the inlined dictionary code.
